cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I clapped when you clapped. I've told everyone the gazebo fire was part of the entertainment; Grandad doesn't need complaints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was clapping for the magician. Grandad set fire to the gazebo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that part. From now on it's 'Everyone's fine; we're eating indoors.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Grandad's asking me whether he should apologize when he makes his speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to thank everyone for coming indoors. We'll use his words when anyone asks.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies applause and treats a fire as entertainment; B2 exposes the wrong object of applause. A3 masks confusion while D183 drives safe shared wording.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 magician correction prompts A3 indoor-meal account; B4 apology question causes A5 to substitute thanks in the speech.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects a family misconception and B4 relays Grandad's reasonable wish to apologize; A wants to protect his dignity.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes Grandad's speech the source everyone will repeat because B4 gives him that public moment.

specificity.evidence: A1 gazebo fire and Grandad, B2 magician, A3 indoor meal and B4 speech make the party understandable without unseen staging.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 yes that part is a compact face-saving move; A5 requests thanks and reuses those words, without explaining the card.
